title: Karnataka CM and cabinet stage sit-in at state election office
seoTitle: Bengaluru: Karnataka CM's sit-in at poll office

tea.why: The CM alleges BJP agents filed fraudulent Form 7 applications to delete eligible voters during the roll revision.
tea.want: FIRs over the allegedly fraudulent Form 7 deletion requests and a pause of the SIR.
tea.changed: Oct 2–3: BJP leaders asked police to file FIRs against the CM and ministers, saying the sit-in broke protest rules.

summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, cabinet ministers and Congress MLAs staged a sit-in at the office of the state's Chief Electoral Officer in Bengaluru on October 1, postponing a cabinet meeting to do so. They demanded FIRs over what they called fraudulent Form 7 applications seeking the deletion of voters during the Special Intensive Revision; the CM alleged attempts to remove about 10,000 voters in each constituency. The BJP objected: a delegation led by Leader of the Opposition R. Ashoka asked the Bengaluru police commissioner to register FIRs against the CM and ministers, arguing that a High Court order makes Freedom Park the only designated protest venue. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi said the CM should focus on drought and farmers and questioned whether permission had been taken.
demands: FIRs over allegedly fraudulent Form 7 deletion applications
Removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar (Congress demand)
response: No response from the Election Commission is reported in these sources. BJP leaders asked police to register FIRs against the CM and ministers for protesting outside the designated venue.

updates.text: The CM, ministers and MLAs held a sit-in at the Chief Electoral Officer's office in Bengaluru.
A BJP delegation asked the police commissioner to file FIRs against the CM and ministers.
Union Minister Pralhad Joshi questioned whether the protest had permission.
